questions.question_text: An architect enters into a contract with an engineering company to provide architectural design services. The architect hires five employees to assist with delivering the project. The engineering company loses its construction licence and cannot pay the architect. As a result, the architect cannot pay their employees their wages. Which situation best describes the architect’s personal liability to pay the employees’ wages?
options: The architect has no personal liability. The employees will need to sue the architect’s business for payment of wages due.
As a sole trader, the architect has limited liability, which means the architect does not have to pay the wages from their own assets.
The architect is operating an incorporated body because the architect hired employees.
The architect and the employees are in partnership together and each has personal liability for the wages.
As a sole trader, the architect is personally liable for the employees' salaries.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A company is experiencing temporary cash flow problems and for the past 4 months has been unable to pay the instalments as they fall due on a bank loan. Based on the available facts, which of the following best describes the position of the company and its shareholders?
options: The shareholders and the company are liable for the amount owed to the bank.
Only those shareholders who are also directors are liable for the amount owed to the bank.
Only the company is liable for the amount owed to the bank.
Only the company is liable for the amount owed to the bank. Neither the shareholders nor the company are liable for the amount owed to the bank.
The shareholders are liable on behalf of the company for the amount owed to the bank.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: Three clients decide to go into business together. They each invest equal amounts of capital in the business and agree to share the profits equally. After 2 years, the business has made a loss and the clients no longer believe the business is viable. Which statement best describes the nature of the three clients’ business?
options: It is a general partnership because they are in business together and intended to make a profit even though they have made a loss.
It is a general partnership, because they agreed to invest equal amounts of capital in the business.
It is not a general partnership, because they have not registered themselves as a partnership.
It is not a general partnership, because they have not entered into a partnership agreement.
It is possibly a general partnership, provided that was their stated intention.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A director of a cosmetics company ordered palm oil for use in the company’s products but made fraudulent representations about the company’s ability to pay £1.2 million for the shipment. The company’s inability to pay was not discovered until after the goods had been shipped due to the director deliberately concealing financial information about the company. Which of the following statements best describes the legal position?
options: The principle of separate legal personality can be disregarded and the director held personally liable due to the director’s fraud and dishonesty.
The principle of separate legal personality means only the company can be held liable.
The principle of separate legal personality means the director cannot be held personally liable for the debt.
The principle of separate legal personality means only the company and its shareholders can be held liable.
The principle of separate legal personality means the director cannot be held personally liable for the debt until the company becomes insolvent.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A shareholder buys 1000 £1 shares in a limited company and pays £850 for the shares in April. In July, the company goes into insolvent liquidation. Which statement best represents the shareholder’s financial obligation on insolvency for the unpaid amount on the shares?
options: As a shareholder in a limited liability company, the investor will not have to pay anything.
The shareholder will have to pay £1,000.
The shareholder will have to pay £850.
The shareholder will not have to pay the unpaid amount of £150 because the company is now insolvent.
The shareholder will have to pay £150.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: The sole shareholder in a company that buys and sells books online decided to insure the books against water damage. The shareholder took out the insurance policy in their own name. Some months later the company’s warehouse housing its books flooded. The shareholder claimed for a pay out under the insurance policy. Which of the following best describes the insurance company’s likely response to the claim?
options: The insurance company will decline the shareholder’s claim on the grounds that the policy should have been in the name of at least one director.
The insurance company will sue the shareholder for misrepresentation.
The insurance company will decline the shareholder’s claim on the grounds that the books belonged to the company.
The insurance company will pay the insurance monies to the shareholder.
The insurance company will pay out as the shareholder was the sole shareholder of the company.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: Which one of the following best describes a limited liability partnership?
options: A corporate body whose members are jointly and severally liable.
A relationship between persons carrying on a business with a view to making a profit.
The members contract in their own names and have joint and severally liability.
A corporate body formed by one or more members with a separate legal personality.
A corporate body with a separate legal personality formed by two or more members.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: An adviser is asked to set up a new limited company as part of a wider transaction. They are also asked to be the promoter of the new company and for that role to include entering into contracts of supply on the company’s behalf prior to it being formed. The adviser is concerned about the possible legal implications of this role. Which statement below best describes liability under a pre-incorporation contract entered into by the adviser?
options: Both the company being incorporated and the promoter have potential liability under the pre-incorporation contract.
The promoter potentially has personal liability under the pre- incorporation contract.
A promoter is in the same position as a shareholder and has limited liability.
No liability falls on the promoter under a pre-incorporation contract.
The company being incorporated has liability under the pre- incorporation contract.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: Two investors buy shares in a private limited company. The company send them information including a note on payment of dividends and the company’s role in maintenance of its own share capital. Which of the following best describes the effect of the maintenance of capital doctrine on the investors’ money?
options: The money invested has to be placed on deposit to guarantee its eventual return to company investors.
The money invested must be reserved for the benefit of creditors if the company becomes insolvent.
The money invested has to be reinvested to guarantee a return for the company.
The money invested cannot be used for any purpose other than repaying creditors.
The money invested will be returned to investors on request.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.1_ Business organisations_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A partnership is set up to provide interior design services. Soon after the business commences, a written partnership agreement is signed. No partners have left or joined the partnership. The partners would like to know at what point they actually became partners in this venture.Which statement best reflects their position as to when they became partners?
options: When they signed their written partnership agreement
When they started trading by selling their design services
When they first shared profits generated by the business
When they hired premises and selected a business name
When they started to carry on a business together in common
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Some entrepreneurs have each been operating as sole traders and have decided to join forces for a limited period during which they will complete a one-off joint venture. They will operate this business as a partnership that will run only until the project is completed. The entrepreneurs acknowledge that it will be essential for the success of this venture that they all share equally in any profits, have equal liability and all play a full and active role in its management. You have advised them that they should have a written partnership agreement.Which statement best reflects why they should have a written partnership agreement?
options: The partners will be able to share profits and losses equally.
It is important to ensure that all the default provisions as to profit share and management under the Partnership Act 1890 have been excluded.
They should ensure that the partnership is not deemed to be “at will” and so terminable on immediate notice.
They should ensure that all the default provisions as to profit share and management under the Partnership Act 1890 have been included.
The partners should ensure that they have more than just a right to manage.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Four friends wish to set up a business in partnership and so enter into a written partnership agreement that specifies:- All of them have contributed an equal amount of capital to the business.- Interest is paid on their capital contributions at 5% pa.- All of them share profits and losses equally.- One of the partners is paid a salary of £10,000 pa.Which statement best reflects the friends’ position under the Partnership Act 1890?
options: They have excluded the default provisions under the Partnership Act 1890 in relation to the payment of a salary only.
They have excluded the default provisions under the Partnership Act 1890 in relation to their capital investment.
They have excluded all of the default provisions under the Partnership Act 1890.
They have excluded the default provisions under the Partnership Act 1890 in relation to the payment of interest on capital and the payment of a salary.
They have excluded none of the default provisions of the Partnership Act 1890.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Three friends are partners in a partnership. All profits and losses are shared equally and they all contributed an equal amount in capital to start the business. In order to expand the business, the partners approach their bank with a view to securing a loan of £90,000. The bank agrees to the loan, charging interest at 15% pa. Unfortunately, after a year, the partnership fails and the bank wants to enforce the terms of the loan.Which statement best reflects the position of the partnership?
options: Each partner will be required to contribute £30,000 to repay the bank.
This is a partnership debt and so the partnership’s assets will be realised and used to pay back the bank in full.
Each partner could be required to repay the bank in full in respect of the total borrowing and any outstanding interest.
Each partner will be required to contribute £30,000 and their share of any outstanding interest payments to repay the bank.
This is a partnership debt and so the bank will not be able to require the partners to contribute personally, unless it requested personal guarantees from each of them.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partnership operates under a written agreement that specifies that the partnership will continue for a fixed period of 5 years. After 3 years have elapsed, one of the partners would like to retire from the partnership. Which statement best reflects the partner’s position?
options: The partner cannot leave the partnership during the fixed term without the consent of their fellow partners to vary the agreement to permit retirement.
The partner can leave during the fixed term by giving a period of reasonable notice to their fellow partners.
As it is a fixed term partnership, the partner cannot leave until the fixed period ends.
The partner could terminate the partnership by giving notice with immediate effect.
The partnership is at will and so the partner can retire from the continuing partnership.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: All three partners in a new partnership agree to make initial capital contributions as follows:A = £30,000B = £35,000C = £25,000In addition, B will loan the partnership an additional £10,000. They have not yet entered into a written partnership agreement. Which statement best reflects the partners’ position?
options: Partner B is entitled to interest but at a maximum rate of 5% in respect of the loan.
The payment of interest on capital is not permitted although Partner B will be entitled to interest of 5% on the loan.
The partners must share profits and losses equally.
A written partnership agreement could provide for both interest on capital and on the loan at a rate chosen by the partners, but in default Partner B would be entitled to interest of 5% on the loan.
All three partners will be entitled to 5% on their capital investment but Partner B will not be entitled to interest on the loan.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Five people have been working together on a business project to develop software. No agreement was ever signed in relation to the project. They all agreed to share their existing knowledge and technology and had their own area of responsibility for developing the project. They each invested different amounts and agreed to share profits in proportion to their capital contributions. Before they could produce the software, two of the people had a disagreement and now want to end their involvement in the project.Which one of the following statements best describes whether a partnership existed between these five individuals?
options: There was no partnership because they invested unequal amounts in the business and failed to register the partnership.
There was no partnership because they did not have a written partnership agreement.
There was a partnership agreement, because each person was assigned an area of responsibility and they shared their knowledge and technology.
There was no partnership because the partnership was dissolved before any profits were made.
There was a partnership because they were carrying on a business in common with a view to making a profit.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: In a partnership with no written agreement, one partner believes they work more hours in the firm than any of the other partners. The aggrieved partner asks the other partners for a salary in compensation for the additional work. The other partners refuse and so the aggrieved partner gives notice to the firm that they will be leaving the partnership with immediate effect.Which statement best reflects the status of the partnership in light of the notice?
options: The entire partnership will end as a result of the notice.
The aggrieved partner may leave once all the partners agree to their departure by a majority vote and determine their notice period.
The aggrieved partner does not have a valid reason for leaving, as partners are only allowed a share in profits not salaries, so therefore the notice is ineffective.
The aggrieved partner may leave with immediate effect and may have a valid claim for constructive dismissal.
The other partners can carry on the partnership on the same terms, provided they buy out the departing partner’s share of the partnership.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Two partners have been running a business. One partner contributed more to financing the business when it was set up, but they agreed that all decisions relating to the business would be made by unanimous consent. Apart from this, they did not discuss any other terms of running the business.Which one of the following statements represents the correct position regarding running the partnership?
options: To bring the partnership to an end, a month’s notice is required.
Each partner’s liability is limited to their contribution in the business.
The two partners will share profits equally.
If both partners decide to introduce a third partner, the new partner will become liable for the existing debts of the business.
If one partner gives notice of their intention to retire from the business, the other partner can continue to run it.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partnership owns and manages two wine bars. It has transpired that one of the partners also works as a part-time cook for a primary school to supplement their income. There is no partnership agreement. The partnership seeks your advice on whether the partner is required to devote their full time and attention to their partnership, and whether they must account for their wages from the primary school to the partnership.Which one of the following statements offers the best advice?
options: Although the partner cannot work for the primary school at the same time as being a partner, they will not have to account for their wages to the partnership.
The partner can work for the primary school but must account for their wages to the partnership.
The partner will be required to account for up to half their wages from the primary school to the partnership.
The partner cannot work for the primary school at the same time as being a partner and may have to account for their wages to the partnership.
The partner can work for the primary school and will not have to account for their wages to the partnership.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.2: Partnership agreement: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

bus7.3.stem: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: All the partners in a trading partnership unanimously vote that, until they all agree otherwise, they will not make any new purchases with a value over £10,000 due to cash-flow difficulties. A month later one of the partners is offered a “bargain” item of equipment for £15,000 by one of the partnership’s regular suppliers. That partner bought it immediately, claiming there was no time to consult the others, and justified the purchase by stating it would help the partnership generate greater profits. Did the partner have actual authority from their fellow partners to make this purchase and which statement best reflects the position?
options: No, because of the unanimous decision setting a spending limit.
Yes, because the partner was dealing with a supplier who knew them to be a partner.
No, but the partner would have had implied authority because this was a regular supplier and the item related to the partnership business.
No, because a regular supplier would know about the spending limit.
Yes, because the purchase relates to the firm’s business.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partnership has three partners, one of whom has set up a competing venture in their “spare time”. The two other partners would like to expel the competing partner and continue in business. There is no written partnership agreement and so it operates as a partnership at will. Which statement best reflects the position?
options: The competing partner can only be expelled if they consent to their own expulsion.
It is never possible to expel a partner from an ongoing partnership.
The competing partner can be expelled, because they are in breach of their fiduciary duty not to compete with the partnership.
The non-competing partners can apply to the court on the grounds that it would be just and equitable to expel the competing partner.
A partner can always be expelled by a simple majority.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A former partner would like to be discharged from their pre-retirement partnership liabilities, which have been incurred under various contracts with the partnership’s existing suppliers. The partnership is continuing with the remaining partners. Which statement best describes who would need to agree to novate these contracts to achieve the former partner’s goal?
options: Any new partners recruited to the partnership
The former partner, the ongoing partners and the existing suppliers
The former partner and the existing suppliers
Anyone who was a partner at the date of the former partner’s retirement
The existing suppliers
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A previously successful partnership was dissolved by order of the court on the ground that it can only be carried on at a loss due to the sudden liquidation of its only significant customer. There was no written partnership agreement. Which one of the following best reflects what will be applied first to pay any sums owed by the partnership that were incurred prior to its dissolution?
options: The partners’ capital investments in the partnership
Any profits of the partnership
Any loans made to the partnership
The personal assets of the partners who made the dissolution application
The partners' personal assets
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partner retires from an ongoing partnership. The partner wants to ensure that they will not be liable, after their retirement, for any future partnership debt incurred with the partnership’s many suppliers. The retiring partner has already asked that their name is removed from all the firm’s publicity materials, invoices and other documents. Which statement best describes what other action (if anything) the retiring partner should take to minimise any further liability to the partnership’s suppliers?
options: The retiring partner should advertise locally.
There is no need to do anything further, as long as the retiring partner does not hold themselves out as a partner.
The retiring partner should place a notice in the London Gazette.
The retiring partner should ask for an indemnity from their fellow partners.
The retiring partner should ensure that each supplier has had actual notice that they have left the partnership.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partner is retiring from their firm and gives notice of their retirement to the remaining partners. In the notice the partner states that, once retired, they will have no further liability for any partnership debts. The remaining partners are concerned because the partnership owes money to various suppliers and has an existing loan with a bank. There was no written agreement between the partners. Which of the following best describes the retiring partner’s liability for the partnership debts?
options: The retiring partner is not liable for the existing debts, because they were taken into account when calculating the retiring partner’s share when they were bought out by the remaining partners.
The remaining partners are now solely responsible for the debts owed to the suppliers and the bank.
The retiring partner will remain liable for the partnership debts because the debts were incurred before their retirement.
The retiring partner is not liable for the existing debts or any future liabilities incurred by the firm to third parties.
The retiring partner will not be liable for the debts provided they put a notice in the London Gazette and ensure their name is removed from all the partnership’s stationery.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partner in a bakery places an order for designer clothes on credit in the name of the firm without consulting the other partners. The clothing company knows the partnership is a bakery business but assumes the partner is authorised to make the order and ships the clothes. The partner forgets to settle the invoice and the clothing company wants to know who to pursue for the outstanding sum. Which statement below represents the correct legal position?
options: The partner cannot be held personally liable because they were acting in their capacity as a partner and the clothing company extended credit to the firm.
As the contract for the designer clothes has no apparent connection with the firm’s business, the firm is unlikely to be held liable.
The clothing company can sue the partner personally to recover the outstanding sum because the transaction relates to the type of business in which the bakery is engaged.
The clothing company will need to write off the sum as it did not undertake proper due diligence.
Each of the partners in the bakery can be pursued for the outstanding sum because the partner bound all of them jointly and severally.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Your client is one of three partners in a business that paves commercial driveways. They do not have a written partnership agreement. While on holiday, your client stayed in a hotel and struck a deal with the hotel owner to pave its driveway. The partner earned a profit of £12,000 and deposited this into their personal bank account without telling the other partners. Which statement best represents the correct legal position regarding your client’s activity?
options: The work that was carried out was unrelated to the business so your client may retain the profits.
If the hotel owner can prove that the work on the driveway is defective, they can sue the partnership for damages.
Provided your client pays their income tax liabilities, the other two partners have no right to know anything about what your client does in their spare time.

If the other partners find out, they could decide to remove your client from the partnership on the basis that your client engaged in a competing business but if they do so, they will not be able to claim the profit for the partnership.
Your client will be responsible for disclosing to the other two partners the amount of profit they made on holiday and should be prepared to share the profit with them.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A partner has retired from an ongoing partnership having been a partner in it for some years. They still work part-time on a consultancy basis for the partnership, fulfilling a very similar role to that which they held as a partner. When they retired, they informed all existing clients that they were retiring and also advertised in the London Gazette. Which statement most accurately describes the retired partner’s position?
options: The partner will only risk personal liability if they represent themselves to be a partner.
The retired partner could be at risk of “holding out” thereby risking personal liability for all partnership debt.
The retired partner could be at risk of “holding out” thereby risking personal liability in respect of debts where a third party was misled as to the retired partner’s status.
The retired partner will still be a partner and so will be jointly and severally liable for all partnership debt.
The retired partner is at no risk as they have informed both existing clients and the wider world that they have retired.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.3: Partners' responsibilities and liability: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

bus7.4.stem: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Three entrepreneurs plan to incorporate a private limited company as the vehicle for their new business giving paddleboard and kayaking lessons. They will all be shareholders and directors. The first entrepreneur becomes aware of a “too good to miss” deal on a bulk order of paddleboards. They are keen to proceed as the deal is only open for 24 hours but are concerned about incurring any personal liability. Which of the following would be most likely to achieve the first entrepreneurs required aims?
options: The first entrepreneur can avoid personal liability as this will be a pre- incorporation contract and so will be void.
The first entrepreneur can proceed, and will not be personally liable, as the company, when formed, will be able to novate the contract with the supplier unilaterally.
The first entrepreneur can avoid personal liability if the other two entrepreneurs also sign the pre-incorporation contract with the supplier.
The first entrepreneur can avoid liability as long as they tell the supplier they are placing the order on behalf of the new company.
The first entrepreneur can avoid personal liability if they purchase a shelf company which can enter into the contract with the supplier.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Two businesspeople are forming a private limited company. They have decided it will adopt the Model Articles for private limited companies in their entirety and without amendment. Which of the following must be supplied to the Registrar of Companies (at Companies House) to complete the registration process?
options: Articles of association, memorandum and Form IN01
Memorandum and Form IN01
Form IN01
Articles of association and Form IN01
Memorandum and articles of association
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A sole trader has decided to incorporate their business as a private limited company and plans to be the only subscriber to the memorandum of association. Which of the following best describes the proposed new company?
options: The sole trader cannot be both the company’s sole shareholder and director.
The sole trader can be the company’s sole director, only shareholder and, if it opts to have one, its company secretary.
The sole trader can be the company’s sole director and only shareholder.
The sole trader can be the company’s sole director and shareholder, but someone other than the sole trader must be appointed as its company secretary.
The new company must have at least two directors.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: If a private limited company was incorporated in March, what will be the date of its accounting reference date (ARD) annually?
options: 31 March
31 December
1 April
1 March
1 January
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Two business associates have acquired a private limited company “off the shelf”. It is incorporated with the relevant Model Articles unamended and they receive the certificate of incorporation. Which of the following would now need to be filed at Companies House to change the company’s name to one they find more suitable for the purposes of their new business?
options: Form NM01
Form IN01 and a special resolution of its members
Forms IN01, NM01 and a special resolution of its members
Form NM01 and a special resolution of its members
Form IN01
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: The promoters of a private limited company are trying to decide on its corporate name for the purposes of incorporation. Which one of the following suffixes (if any) must be included after its chosen name on the Form IN01?
options: LLP
There is no need for anything to appear after the name of a private limited company, as long as the name is not offensive or the same as one on the register at Companies House
plc
& Co
ltd
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Entrepreneurs have acquired a private limited company off the shelf from their solicitors. Which one of the following best describes what must happen for them to commence operating their new business?
options: Replace the first director(s) and shareholder(s).
Increase the company’s share capital.
Change the company’s registered office.
Change the company’s place of registration.
Change the company’s name.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A company, with four directors, has been incorporated using the Model Articles with one amendment: the quorum for board meetings has been raised to three (Model Article 11 disapplied). There are two separate proposals at the first board meeting. One of the directors is an interested director in one of them and another director is an interested director in the other. Which one of the following correctly reflects the position in relationship to the company’s decision-making?
options: The articles will need to be amended to reduce the quorum and to permit interested directors to vote.
Any director can vote as long as it is for the benefit of the company.
The directors will be able to approve both matters although the two interested directors must abstain from voting when they are personally interested.
The two interested directors will be interested and so cannot vote or count towards the quorum on either matter.
The articles will need to be amended to permit interested directors to vote.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.4: Incorporation of a company: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Your client is keen to invest in a new private limited company. They have been offered a number of shares in the company and wish to understand the significance of a shareholder’s role in a private limited company. Which one of the following statements best describes your client’s role as a shareholder?
options: They will be one of the owners of the company involved in certain key decisions and rewarded by way of dividend, if profits allow.
They will be one of the owners of the company involved in the day-to- day running of the company and be paid a salary.
They will be an adviser to the company on key decisions and rewarded by way of dividends, if profits allow.
They will be one of the owners of the company and rewarded by way of a dividend, if profits allow, but with no ability to influence the running of the company.
They will be an adviser to the company on key decisions and be paid a salary.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A medical supplies private limited company has two directors, who are also shareholders of the company with shareholdings of 70% and 20% respectively. A third shareholder owns a 10% share of the company. The two directors have been very keen on developing relationships with pharmacies in their locality. Unfortunately, they have been rather slow in calling in debts owed for goods supplied months ago. They have taken the unusual decision of writing off certain debts owed to the company, on the basis that they would not wish to sour future business relationships with those clients. The minority shareholder has been receiving lower dividend payments recently and is very concerned to learn about the directors’ decision not to chase certain outstanding debts. Which ONE of the following statements best describes the minority shareholder’s position?
options: The minority shareholder does not have any legal basis to raise an unfair prejudice claim, as a claim can only be raised after all other means of recourse have been exhausted.
The minority shareholder only holds a 10% shareholding, which is too low to have access to any minority shareholder remedies.
The minority shareholder has various remedies such as an action for unfair prejudice which they can seek if they feel the company is not being run for their benefit.
The minority shareholder cannot raise a claim for any remedy as it is only the company – as a separate legal person – that can ever raise such a claim.
The doctrine of majority rule means the minority shareholder should not make a claim for any remedy such as unfair prejudice.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A promoter is incorporating a new private limited company and is investigating the statutory requirements for share registration. The articles of the company provide for one class of share and no pre-emption rights. There are two subscribers to the new company and the plan is then to allot shares to a new shareholder within 6 months of incorporation. Which statement best describes when the two subscribers and the subsequent shareholder will become members of the company?
options: The two subscribers will become members on receipt of the forms required for registration of the company at Companies House. The subsequent shareholder will become a member when their name is entered in the register of members.

The two subscribers will become members on registration of the company when their names are entered in the register of members. The subsequent shareholder will become a member when their name is entered in the register of members.
The two subscribers will become members on registration of the company. The subsequent shareholder will become a member following the passing of a board resolution on allotment.
The two subscribers will become members on registration of the company. The subsequent shareholder will become a member on the filing of the return of allotments with Companies House.

The two subscribers will become members at the first general meeting following registration of the company. The subsequent shareholder will become a member on the filing of the return of allotments with Companies House.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A private limited company has four shareholders, with holdings of 10%, 10%, 30% and 50% respectively. The board has been notified of the requirement to maintain a register for shareholders who have significant control within the company. They seek advice on the practical implications of this requirement for the company, given the current shareholdings. Which of the following is the most accurate summary of the current requirements on the company for entry on their PSC register?
options: None of the shareholders is currently required to be entered into the PSC register but the company must maintain a PSC register.
Only the shareholders with holdings of 30% and 50% respectively are required to be entered into the PSC register with the required statement relating to their shareholding.

Only the shareholders with holdings of 30% and 50% respectively are required to give their consent for their interest in shares to be entered into the PSC register with the required statement relating to their shareholding.
Only the shareholder with a 50% holding is required to be entered into the PSC register with the required statement relating to their shareholding.
All the shareholders, given their size of shareholding, need to be entered into the PSC register with the required statement relating to their shareholding.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Four shareholders of a private limited company wish to work together to address issues of deadlock, financing and voting within general meetings of the company. Two of those shareholders are also directors of the company and are exploring what they as directors could agree to vote on at board level and whether this should be documented. The four shareholders ask for advice on what sort of agreement they can put in place, should the company be a party to their agreement, and if it is a requirement for any such agreement to be filed at Companies House along with the articles of association. Which statement best describes your advice to the shareholders on these points?
options: A company must be a party to a shareholder agreement; the company is not required to file the shareholder agreement at Companies House as it is a private contract. The two directors can agree to terms within that agreement that would determine how they would vote as shareholders and directors.

A company must be a party to a shareholder agreement; the company is also required to file the shareholder agreement at Companies House as it is a public document. The two directors cannot agree to terms within that shareholder agreement that would determine how they would vote as directors.

A company can voluntarily be a party to a shareholder agreement; the company is not required to file the shareholder agreement at Companies House as it is a private contract. The two directors cannot agree to terms within that agreement that would determine how they would vote as directors.

A company can voluntarily be a party to a shareholder agreement; the company is not required to file the shareholder agreement at Companies House as it is a private contract. The two directors can agree to terms within that agreement that would determine how they would vote as shareholders and directors.

A company can voluntarily be a party to a shareholder agreement; the company is however required to file the shareholder agreement at Companies House as it is a public document. The two directors cannot agree to terms within that agreement that would determine how they would vote as directors.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: Two shareholders, who together hold 10% of the shares in a private limited company, wish to take action against a director whom they are accusing of breach of duty. The shareholders have petitioned the board, but the majority of directors on the board refuse to take any action. The shareholders understand that they have rights as minority shareholders and, having reviewed possible actions, decide to undertake a statutory derivative claim. In view of these facts, which of the following best summarises the statutory derivative claim?
options: Directors adopt the claim for the shareholders in the company’s name for a wrong committed against the company. A director brings the claim, but it vests in the company and any monies recovered go to the company.

Shareholders bring the claim in the company’s name for a wrong committed against the company. Shareholders bring the claim, it vests in the shareholders and any monies recovered go to the shareholders.

Directors adopt the claim for the shareholders in the company’s name for a wrong committed against the company. A director brings the claim, it vests in the shareholders and any monies recovered go to the shareholders.
The board brings the claim in the name of the company for a wrong committed against the company. A director brings the claim, but it vests in the company and any monies recovered go to the company.
Shareholders bring the claim in the company’s name for a wrong committed against the company. A shareholder brings the claim, but it vests in the company and any monies recovered go to the company.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A shareholder/director has brought a successful action for unfair prejudice action against a private limited company and obtained a court order, setting out alterations to the articles of association. A second shareholder would like to obtain a copy of the company’s current articles of association, the director’s service contract and any company board minutes relating to the unfair prejudice action. Which statement provides the best summary of the second shareholder’s rights in this regard?
options: The company can accept or decline a request by any member to send them a copy of the items requested, although no fee can be charged.

The company can refuse to send any constitutional documents to the member and instead should suggest they obtain them direct from Companies House, as the articles and any resolutions affecting the articles are public documents. The company is not required under the Companies Act 2006 to send them board minutes or the director’s service contract.
The company can decline a request by any member to send them a copy of the board minutes. The other items must be supplied on payment of a reasonable fee.

The company must, on request by any member, send them a copy of the company's current articles and the director’s service contract. No fee should be charged. The company is not required under the Companies Act 2006 to send them any board minutes.

The company must, on request by any member, send them a copy of the company's current articles and its board meeting minutes without charge, A copy of the service contract can only be supplied with the consent of the relevant director, who is entitled to a reasonable fee.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: The articles of a private limited company provide for one class of share and no pre-emption rights. Two shareholders were allotted some new shares by the company. One of the shareholders also transferred some shares to the other shareholder. They ask your advice on when they will receive their share certificates and own the shares. Which of the following summaries most accurately describes the shareholders’ position?
options: Shareholders are entitled to receive a share certificate from the company within 2 months of allotment, if freshly issued or when the transfer is lodged with the company. Only when the shareholders’ names are entered on the register do they become a shareholder.

Shareholders are entitled to receive a share certificate from the company within 6 weeks of allotment, if freshly issued or when the transfer is lodged with the company. Only when the share certificate is received do they become a shareholder.

Shareholders are entitled to receive a share certificate from the company within 1 month of allotment, if freshly issued or when the transfer is lodged with the company. Only when the shareholders’ names are entered on the register do they become a shareholder.

Shareholders are entitled to receive a share certificate from the company within 2 weeks of allotment, if freshly issued or when the transfer is lodged with the company. Only when the share certificate is received do they become a shareholder.

Shareholders are entitled to receive a share certificate from the company within 1 month of allotment, if freshly issued or within 2 months of the transfer being lodged with the company. Only when the share certificate is received do they become a shareholder.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

questions.question_text: A minority shareholder who owns over 10% of the company’s shares is very unhappy at the direction the company is being taken. They have fallen out with the board of directors and is now being excluded from management despite previous agreements to the contrary. Although they think some other minority shareholders may agree with them and vote with them in General Meeting, they would like to realise their investment (the company is profitable), so that they can start a new venture. Unfortunately, the directors will not respond to their requests to discuss buying their shares. Which statement best reflects the position?
options: The shareholder should demand a poll vote at general meeting.
The shareholder should bring a derivative claim.
The shareholder should circulate written representations to the other shareholders.
The shareholder should commence a claim of unfair prejudice.
The shareholder should instigate the winding-up of the company under the just and equitable principle.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.5: Shareholder rights: Ghita Bennis (She:Her)

bus7.6.stem: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A company is incorporated with the Model Articles as its articles of association. There are four shareholders of the company, each holding a 25% share. One of the directors has now retired and the board is seeking advice on the appointment of a replacement director. Which statement set out below most accurately reflects the procedure the board should follow under the Model Articles to appoint a new director?
options: The board approves the appointment of the new director and the shareholders approve by special resolution.
The new appointment can be made by ordinary resolution of the members or by a majority decision of the directors.
The shareholders can pass a special resolution to appoint the new director without recourse to the board.
The board has sole authority to appoint a new director (who must hold shares in the company) by a majority and can pass a board resolution to that effect.
The board has sole authority to appoint a new director and can pass a board resolution to that effect.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A director of a company, who is appointed at incorporation, persuades the four shareholders to include the director’s name in the articles of association as a “life” director. Several years later, the director has fallen out with three of the shareholders, who together hold 90% of the voting share capital. The shareholders seek to remove the director from their role against the director’s will. The director seeks your advice on their position. What is the director’s position under the Companies Act?
options: As a named “life” director, the director can only be removed by the shareholders passing a special resolution after receiving special notice of 21 days under the Companies Act.
To remove the director, under the Companies Act shareholders must give special notice of 28 days to the company and if agreed, pass a written resolution for the director's removal.
As a named “life” director, the director’s position is “entrenched” and they cannot be removed as a director by the shareholders under the Companies Act.

To remove the director, under the Companies Act shareholders must give special notice of 21 days directly to the director, hold a general meeting to discuss the director’s removal and if agreed, pass an ordinary resolution for the director's removal.

To remove the director, under the Companies Act the shareholders must give special notice of 28 days to the company, hold a general meeting to discuss the director’s removal and if agreed, pass an ordinary resolution for the director's removal.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A director (who also holds 5% of shares in the company) receives special notice of a resolution to secure their removal at a general meeting. They ask you for advice on the remedies they might seek against the company if the resolution for removal is passed by the shareholders. Which is the most accurate summary of the remedies the director might seek if removed from their position as director?
options: The director has no entitlement to damages or compensation for loss of office but may be able to claim for unfair prejudice.
The director will receive no compensation for loss of office but may be entitled to damages for any unlawful termination of any service contract.
The director may be entitled to damages for unlawful termination of any service contract and compensation for loss of office, and may have a possible claim for unfair prejudice.
The director’s service contact can be terminated without payment of any damages by way of compensation, but the director can receive a nominal sum for loss of office.

The director has no status for a claim for unfair prejudice (as the company is the proper claimant) or damages due to any unlawful termination of any service contract, but retains the right to possible compensation for loss of office.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A director of a struggling company is aware that the company is unable to pay its creditors’ invoices and that all the board members have been criticised for their handling of company finances. The director is concerned that they may be involved in court proceedings and in particular be charged with being unfit to be involved in company management. Which of the following best summarises the factors that guide whether and for how long an order can be made by the court in relation to the director?
options: Whether they were a director of a company which becomes insolvent after they were a director, in which case the minimum disqualification period is 2 years and the maximum disqualification period is 10 years.

Whether they were a director of a company which becomes insolvent before, while or after they were a director, in which case the minimum disqualification period is 2 years and the maximum disqualification period is 15 years.

Whether they were a director and shareholder of a company which becomes insolvent after they were a director and shareholder, in which case the minimum disqualification period is 2 years and the maximum disqualification period is 10 years.

Whether they were a director of a company which becomes insolvent while they were a director, in which case the minimum disqualification period is 2 years and the maximum disqualification period is 15 years.

Whether they were a director of a company which becomes insolvent while or after they were a director, in which case the minimum disqualification period is 2 years and the maximum disqualification period is 15 years.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A 4-year disqualification order is imposed on a director of a limited company, after persistent failure to file returns with the Registrar of Companies. However, the director continues to be involved in ongoing management duties in the company. What are the potential consequences for the director of their ongoing involvement?
options: The director is committing a criminal offence and may face personal liability for debts which the company incurs while the director is involved in its management management or be required to make payment by way of a compensation order/undertaking.
The director incurs an automatic lifetime disqualification order and may face personal liability for debts which the company incurs while the director is involved in its management.

The director incurs an automatic 4-year extension of the original disqualification order and may face criminal liability for debts which the company incurs while the director is involved in its management.
The director is committing a civil offence and may face both a fine and an automatic 4-year extension of the original disqualification order.
The director is committing a civil offence and may face civil liability for debts which the company incurs while the director is involved in its management.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A group of shareholders in a private limited company proposes to use the relevant procedure under the Companies Act to remove one of the directors. They wish to understand the procedural requirement to provide “special notice”. Which of the following best summarises the requirements of “special notice”?
options: It provides 28 clear days’ notice of an intention to remove a particular director, delivered to the company who in turn must provide a copy of the notice to that director. The director is entitled to attend any subsequent general meeting and speak to the resolution on their removal.

It provides 21 clear days’ notice of an intention to remove a particular director, delivered to the company who in turn must provide a copy of the notice to that director. The director is entitled to attend any subsequent general meeting, whether a shareholder or not, but cannot speak to the resolution on their removal unless they are a shareholder.

It provides 28 clear days’ notice of an intention to remove a particular director, delivered to the company who in turn must provide a copy of the notice to that director. The director (if a shareholder) is entitled to attend any subsequent general meeting and speak to the resolution on their removal.

It provides 21 clear days’ notice of an intention to remove a particular director, and the notice is delivered directly to that director. The director is entitled to attend any subsequent general meeting and speak to the resolution on their removal.

It provides 28 clear days’ notice of an intention to remove a particular director and the notice is delivered directly to that director. The director is entitled to attend any subsequent general meeting but may only provide written representations for discussion at the relevant general meeting.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A private limited company with Model Articles as provided by the Companies Act is appointing a new director to their existing board. You are asked to advise the board on their approach to determining aspects of renumeration and the term of any service contract. Which statement below most accurately summarises key governance rules for the board in their consideration of any terms of a director’s service contract?
options: The board has the authority under the articles as drafted to decide directors’ remuneration and, after any negotiation of the service contract between the director and the company, shareholder approval is required if the contract gives security of tenure for longer than 2 years.

The shareholders and the board have joint authority under the articles as drafted to decide directors’ remuneration and, after any negotiation of the service contract between the director and the company, shareholder approval is required if the contract gives security of tenure for longer than 1 year.

The shareholders have the authority under the articles as drafted to approve directors’ remuneration by ordinary resolution and, after any negotiation of the service contract between the director and the company, shareholder approval is required if the contract gives security of tenure for longer than 2 years.

The chairman of the board has the authority under the articles as drafted to decide directors’ remuneration and, after any negotiation of the service contract between the director and the company, board and shareholder approval is required if the contract gives security of tenure for longer than 2 years.

The chairman of the board has the authority under the articles as drafted to decide directors’ remuneration and, after any negotiation of the service contract between the director and the company, shareholder approval is required if the contract gives security of tenure for longer than 1 year.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A private limited company adopts the Model Articles as provided by the Companies Act. Special notice of a general meeting to remove a director has been given and a general meeting is being held to vote on the resolution to remove the director. Exactly 50% of the votes cast in the meeting are cast for the resolution, the other 50% against. Which of the following summaries best describe the outcome of the vote?
options: A majority (over 50%) of shareholder votes cast at the meeting is needed to pass the resolution. As this threshold has not been reached, the director is suspended from office until another vote is taken on the resolution.
In the event of a tie, the chairman of the general meeting has the casting vote to decide if the director remains in office or is removed from office.
At least 50% of shareholder votes cast at the meeting are needed to pass the resolution. As this threshold has been reached, the director is removed from office.
A majority (over 50%) of shareholder votes cast at the meeting is needed to pass the resolution. As this threshold has not been reached, the director remains in office.
A special majority (75% or over) of shareholder votes cast at the meeting is needed to pass the resolution. As this threshold has not been reached, the director remains in office.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.6_ Directors' appointment and removal_ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: The board of directors of a private limited company has recently received training from their company solicitors on their roles and responsibilities, following a major governance report on the company conducted by independent consultants. The training drew their attention to the duties owed under the Companies Act 2006 and the protection they provide to those who invest in and deal with the company. Which of the following correctly describes to whom the directors of the company owe these duties?
options: The other directors of the company.
The past and present shareholders of the company.
The shareholders of the company.
The employees of the company.
The company.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A company supplying building services to the commercial property industry is struggling financially. In an attempt to save money, one of the two directors has been stalling payments to the company’s suppliers, taking 90 days, rather than 30 days as required by suppliers, to pay outstanding invoices. The director has also delayed payment of employees’ contributions to the tax authority by the company and these are now 6 months overdue. The same director is aware that two of the junior managers are struggling with responsibilities the director has given them, resulting in the need for urgent supervision of their work. The director has been absent for long periods and neglected to give the managers proper induction and training before delegating the new responsibilities to them. The director is concerned as to possible allegations of breach of duty. Given the circumstances what would you advise is the most likely duty to be of concern to the director?
options: The director will be in breach of their duty to exercise independent judgement.
The director will be in breach of their duty to act within powers.
The director will be in breach of their duty not to profit from their directorial position.
The director will be in breach of their duty to exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence.
The director will be in breach of their duty to avoid conflicts of interest.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: Two directors of a private limited company have each independently requested loans of £9000. One director would like their loan to be paid directly to them; the other would like their loan to be paid by the company to their son. Which of the following best describes the company’s obligations in respect of these proposed loans?
options: The company can make the loans to the first director and to the second director’s son, provided they obtain shareholder approvals under s 197 of the Companies Act 2006.
The company can make the loans to the first director and to the second director’s son, provided that they obtain a board resolution, as each of the loans is less than £10,000 in value.
The company can make the loan to the first director with the approval of a board resolution but not to the second director’s son as he is a “connected person”.
The company can make the loan to the first director with the approval of a board resolution and requires a shareholder resolution to approve the loan to the second director’s son.
The company cannot make the loans to either the first director or to the second director’s son as s 197 of the Companies Act 2006 prohibits loans to directors under any circumstances.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: The sales team of a private limited company has recently been put through an intensive process of re-training, due to a slump in the company’s sales performance. During this process, complaints from the sales force about the management style of the Sales Director became the subject of an internal investigation by the Human Resources (HR) team. It is alleged that the director delegates their duties to untrained junior salespeople without supervising them properly. The director’s attendance at sales force meetings is erratic and they are unable to explain the company’s sales markets and sales products coherently at these meetings. The HR team are due to interview the director. Which of the following best summarises the legal implications of the director’s behaviour and the levels of skill and care they should be bringing to their role as a director?
options: The director should be judged on how they carry out their role with the general knowledge, skill and experience that should be expected of someone with the title “Sales Director” and the knowledge and skill that the director actually has as a Sales Director.
The director should not be expected to show a greater degree of skill than their colleagues may reasonably expect from a Sales Director with the director’s actual knowledge and skill.
The director should be judged on how their subordinates carry out their roles and with the general knowledge, skill and experience that the director has passed onto them as a Sales Director.
The director should be judged on how they carry out their role with the general knowledge, skill and experience that should be expected of someone with the title “Sales Director”.

The director should be judged on how their subordinates carry out their roles and on how the director carries out their role with the general knowledge, skill and experience that should be expected of someone with the title “Sales Director”.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A private limited company produces fresh organic fruit. There is a board of six executive directors. A year ago, a second company approached the board and offered to sell the first company a plot of land adjoining one of the first company’s principal market gardens. Due to financial uncertainty and a large debt burden, the board of the first company rejected the proposal. Subsequently, two of the six directors of the first company acted independently and acquired the plot of land for themselves for £250,000. Owing to the recent fall in interest rates and optimistic economic forecasts by the UK Government, the board of the first company regrets its failure to acquire the plot of land and intends to purchase it for the offer price of £350,000. The board of directors of the first company has not been informed who owns the land. If the new sale of the plot of land goes through, which statement best summarises the directors’ duties that will be primarily engaged by the behaviour of the two directors?
options: The two directors will be in potential breach of their duties to exercise independent judgement and not to accept benefits from third parties.
The two directors will be in potential breach of their duties to avoid conflicts of interest and not to accept benefits from third parties.
The two directors will be in potential breach of their duties to act within their powers and avoid conflicts of interest.
The two directors will be in potential breach of their duties to promote the success of the company.
The two directors will be in potential breach of their duties to exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A private limited company provides business solutions for its customers and has three equal shareholders, who are also directors. The company employs 13 staff. One director is committed to equality and diversity best practice and has recently conducted a pay review across the company. The review showed that on average, male employees are paid £8,000 more than their female colleagues, although no breach of the law has occurred. The director called a board meeting to present these facts to the other directors and immediate action has been taken to close the gap. Another director agreed that all pay inequalities should be rectified. However, the third director voted against this decision, which would cost the business £80,000 annually in additional salaries. Which one of following directors’ duties under the Companies Act is most engaged by the board in their discussion of this issue?
options: The duty to promote the success of the company.
The duty to promote the success of the company. The duty to declare an interest in a transaction with the company.
The duty to avoid conflicts of interest.
The duty to exercise independent judgement.
The duty not to accept benefits from third parties.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A small private limited company has five directors on its board, all of whom are also shareholders in the company. Two of the directors are siblings and one of them has been found to have breached their duty to declare an interest in a transaction with the company. The board is discussing ratifying the director’s breach in accordance with the Companies Act 2006 and is taking advice. Which statement best summarises the action the board can take?
options: The director’s conduct can be ratified by a show of hands by the other directors in a board meeting.
The director’s conduct can be ratified by the members in general meeting, but as the two siblings are shareholders, they cannot consent to the resolution for ratification.
The director’s conduct can be ratified if there is a unanimous vote by the board and then ratification by all the members in general meeting.
The director’s conduct cannot be ratified by the members in general meeting as the two siblings are shareholders, and this is an absolute bar to ratification.
The director’s conduct cannot be ratified by the members in general meeting as ratification is only available for breach of trust and negligence.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: A private limited company has given a loan of £16,000 to one director and a loan of £62,000 to a second director, the latter relating to expenditure that director has incurred on the company’s behalf. The board have been notified that, because of the findings of an audit report reported to the annual general meeting, they face potential prosecution for not following the proper procedure regarding directors’ loans and obtaining shareholders’ approval. Which one of the following best summarises the consequences of failing to comply with the procedures relating to directors’ loans?
options: The loans are voidable, if the company chooses, and directors may have to account to the company for any gain they made, as well as indemnifying the company for any loss suffered as a result of the loans being made.
The loans are void due to the breach in procedure and the directors are subject to a fine, as well as indemnifying the company for any loss suffered as a result of the loans being made.

The loans are unaffected by lack of compliance with procedures, provided directors pass a resolution rectifying the failure to comply. Directors may have to account to the company for any gain they made, as well as indemnify the company for any loss suffered as a result of the loans being made.

The loans are void due to the breach in procedure and directors may have to account to shareholders for any gain they made as well as indemnifying the company for any loss suffered as a result of the loans being made.

The loans are voidable, if the company chooses, and directors may have to account to shareholders for any gain they made, as well as indemnifying the company for any loss suffered as a result of the loans being made.
questions.subject: Business Law and Practice
questions.source: BUS7.7_ Directors' duties _ Ghita Bennis (She_Her)

questions.question_text: The directors of a private limited company plan to sell some land, which is owned by the company. The proposed purchaser of the land is known to all the directors and is a parent of one of the directors. The directors are all shareholders in the company. The land has recently been independently valued at £70,000 and the board agrees that this will be the sale price. The company’s most recent set of annual accounts states net profits of £770,000 and net assets of £600,000. The company has adopted the Model Articles (unamended) as its articles of association. Which statement best describes whether the proposed sale of land requires shareholder approval?
options: It does not require shareholder approval, because the transaction falls under the directors’ general authority to manage the company’s business.
It does not require shareholder approval, because the transaction involves the sale and purchase of land, which is a non-cash asset.
It does not require shareholder approval, because the transaction involves the sale and purchase of an asset at its fair market value.

questions.question_text: A solicitor is a partner at a small law firm specialising in personal injury. In handling a case for a client, it becomes clear that a medical report has not been served on the other side. To cover up the mistake, the solicitor backdates a letter and purports to attach the evidence with the dates altered to make it seem that it had been served on time. Despite protests from opposing counsel, the solicitor insists that the evidence was appropriately served. Eventually, the solicitor admits to the firm what has happened. Which of the following statements best describes the professional conduct implications of the solicitor’s actions?
options: The solicitor has breached professional conduct regulations by failing to act with integrity.
The solicitor has breached professional conduct regulations by acting dishonestly.

The solicitor has not breached any conduct regulations as they acted in the best interests of the client by trying to get the evidence on the court file to give the client a chance to proceed with their claim.
The solicitor has breached conduct regulations by failing to act in the best interests of the client.
There are no professional conduct implications as the solicitor has admitted the mistake and the court has not acted on the false evidence.
questions.subject: Ethics and Professional Conduct
questions.source: COND3.2_ Overview of Principles and Codes Part 2

questions.question_text: A solicitor has an appointment for a one-hour case management conference on one of the solicitor’s cases in court at 11.30am on Monday. The case is a substantial and difficult one. It is now Friday afternoon. One of the litigation partners calls into the solicitor’s office and says that they have a case in that same court on Monday. The client is a defendant to a summary judgment application before the District Court judge at 2pm. The hearing is scheduled for one hour. The partner tells the solicitor that the case is entirely straightforward but the file the partner is carrying looks suspiciously thick. The partner makes it clear that they would regard it as a personal favour if the solicitor would take this case on for a very important client. The solicitor’s appraisal is due within the next week or so. Should the solicitor accept the instructions?
options: The solicitor should refuse, as the solicitor must act with independence and integrity.
The solicitor should accept the instructions because this would be the most cost-effective option. The firm will save money by sending just one solicitor instead of two to the same court.
The solicitor should refuse, as the solicitor is unlikely to be able to devote sufficient time to prepare for this case, which would not be in the best interests of the client.
